At the start of this season, I will keep doing what fits my land, water, and labor. I only have 4.1 mu, and my main system is still wheat followed by maize, because that is the most reliable way for me to use the land and the well. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I will keep the plan simple and stable rather than make it too complicated. I will put most of the land into wheat-maize and leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton takes more hand work and more watching through the season. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen first and then support it with phosphorus and potassium, irrigate a few times with the well, and aim for a steady harvest. After wheat, I will plant hybrid maize on the same land because it gives me stronger yield and fits the season well. I will feed maize mainly with nitrogen and give it fewer irrigations than wheat unless the weather is too dry. For cotton, I will keep only a small area, use improved seed, fertilize it moderately, irrigate several times, and control insects carefully because cotton can lose yield fast if I let pests get ahead. I will use rotary tillage for all three because my land is small, it is practical for me, and it saves time.
